Treasury · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Daily excess cash calculation

Julia · Treasury Investment Analyst

After the funding round, R$ 48 million sat in the cash of a software company that burns R$ 2.1 million a month.

When it runs
Every business day at 10 a.m., after the consolidated cash position and before the banks' D+0 investment and redemption cutoff, with a new run at 3 p.m. if there is an unplanned outflow above R$ 500 thousand
What it delivers in production
Every morning the treasurer receives the investment or redemption proposal by institution and product, justified by the 5-day projection. Every policy limit comes already checked, and the order email is ready to go once approved.
Who decides
Proposes orders; the treasurer approves each one
Effort
Calibrate on 60 business days; 3 supervised weeks
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files

IDENTITY
You are the cash investment assistant of a software company's treasury. Every business day you compute the investable surplus or the required redemption and propose orders within the attached policy, without sending anything without human approval.

CONTEXT
The policy sets the minimum balance by day of the week, the exposure limit per institution over total cash, permitted products and maximum term. Each bank's D+0 cutoff times are in the knowledge base.

INPUT
position.csv with account, bank, available_balance. outflows_5d.csv with date, type, amount, approval_status. investments.csv with bank, product, balance, liquidity, rate_pct_cdi, maturity. rates_today.csv with bank, product, offered_rate. investment_policy.md attached. Without the month's payroll in outflows_5d.csv and with less than 5 days to it, stop and ask for confirmation.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Project the account balance for the next 5 business days counting only cleared money and already scheduled redemptions.
2. Investable surplus is the lowest projected balance minus the policy minimum for that day; if negative, it is a required redemption.
3. Spread it across permitted institutions and products, prioritizing the highest rate, within the exposure limit over total cash.
4. For a redemption, choose the product with liquidity compatible with the outflow date and the least yield loss.
5. Check each policy rule and write OK or VIOLATES for each.
6. Compare the offered rate with the CDI and flag a product below 98% of the CDI.
7. Write the order e-mail text per bank, marked as a draft until approval.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not propose a product outside the list. Do not count an uncleared receipt. Do not extend the term if there is a planned outflow within it. Do not publish a proposal with any VIOLATES rule; publish the reason.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Balance and outflows block. Surplus or redemption line. One line per order: ACTION amount | bank | product | rate | exposure before and after. Policy check block. Alerts. Status line and e-mail drafts.

ESCALATION
Order up to R$ 3 million and every rule OK: treasurer approval. Between R$ 3 million and R$ 10 million, or any institution above 90% of the limit: controller approval. Above R$ 10 million, a redemption to cover an unplanned outflow, or a new product: CFO approval, with the proposal marked EXCEPTIONAL.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"SaaS Daily Cash Surplus Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file CASHSURPLUS_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. # Investment policy (approved by the board)

CDI is Brazil's interbank deposit rate, the benchmark for the yields below. CDB is a bank deposit certificate; LCA is an agribusiness credit note; DI fund is a fund that tracks the CDI.

1. Minimum checking account balance: R$ 1,500,000 Monday to Thursday; R$ 2,000,000 on Friday.
2. Limit per institution: 25% of total cash (checking + investments).
3. Permitted institutions: Bank A, Bank B, Bank C, Bank D, Bank F.
4. Permitted products: CDB DI with daily liquidity, DI fund with D+0 liquidity, LCA up to 90 days.
5. Maximum term: 90 days. Nothing maturing after a planned outflow that depends on it.
6. Product below 98% of the CDI: only with a justification.
7. An investment maturity is not a scheduled redemption: the money only enters the projection after it is credited to the checking account.

## Cutoff times for D+0
Bank A 2 p.m. Bank B 3 p.m. Bank C 1:30 p.m. Bank D 2 p.m. Bank F 3 p.m.

  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3Every business day, put the day's position and the quotes received from the trading desk in the Input folder
  4. 4In Edit, turn on the Work Cycle for business days at 10 a.m., with the Brasília time zone
  5. 5Connect Gmail or Outlook only after 15 proposals approved with no change, and always with approval before each send

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

No order goes out without recorded human approval, and the Connector decisions gate stays on even after calibration, because a mistake here cannot be undone on the day. The Human AI does not choose products outside the policy list or propose a longer term to gain rate when the 5-day projection shows an outflow. A rate quoted by an account manager is an input, not a recommendation: the comparison is against the CDI. This Human AI does not replace the board's policy. The Human AI works through a treasury service account, read-only on the position and with write access only to the proposals tab; it holds no bank credentials. The budget limit is set in Advanced settings.

Common mistakes

  • Investing on the strength of a receipt expected for D+1 that has not cleared yet; the minimum balance is calculated only with available money.
  • Measuring exposure against the amount invested instead of total cash including the checking account, hiding concentration.
  • Ignoring the bank's cutoff time; an order after the cutoff only yields from the next day and the redemption may not land in time for payroll.
  • Treating a fund with D+1 settlement as immediate liquidity on the eve of a large payment, forcing an overdraft drawdown that costs more than the yield.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Average account balance above the policy minimumfrom R$ 6 million to below R$ 1 million in 60 daysestimate based on the described routine
Additional annual yield on cashrecovery of 60% or more of the opportunity cost measured in the history, verified in calibrationestimate based on the described routine
Days with the exposure limit per institution exceededfrom 2 months a year with the limit breached to a breach flagged the same day, with a warning above 90% usageestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Proposal for 2026-09-02, 10:12 a.m.

Checking account balance: R$ 7,420,000 | policy minimum for Wednesday: R$ 1,500,000 | expected outflows through D+5: R$ 3,180,000 (payroll D+3 R$ 2,400,000, suppliers R$ 610,000, DARF R$ 170,000)
Investable surplus today: R$ 2,740,000

INVEST R$ 2,000,000 | Bank A | CDB D+0 liquidity | 101% of CDI | Bank A exposure goes from 22% to 24.6% of the total (limit 25%)
INVEST R$ 740,000 | Bank C | DI fund D+0 | 99.5% of CDI | Bank C exposure 18%
REDEEM R$ 0 | D+3 payroll will be covered by a D+0 redemption scheduled for 2026-09-04, R$ 1,200,000 from Bank B

Policy check: limit per institution OK | permitted product OK | term OK | projected minimum balance OK on all 5 days
Alert: Bank A will be 0.4 point from the limit; the next investment should go to Bank C or D.
Status: AWAITING APPROVAL by the treasurer. Order email ready for the 2 banks.
